sources.title: Gilbert Strang, The Wave Equation and Staggered Leapfrog, MIT 18.086 lecture notes, §5.3
sources.locator: Full 11-page §5.3, The Wave Equation and Staggered Leapfrog; PDF pp. 1–10. Read the solution and semidiscrete wave sections, the centered and staggered leapfrog derivation, the Fourier CFL argument, the symmetric first-order-system energy calculation, and the Maxwell equations section.

contents.name: Solution of the Wave Equation
contents.reason: The pair begins with supplied finite matrices and proves their evolution directly; exact continuous-wave solution formulas and characteristic representations are not claims on this page.

contents.name: The Semidiscrete Wave Equation
contents.support: The finite-system definition makes the state vectors, mass matrices, curl map, dissipation and continuous forcing explicit. No particular spatial stencil or continuum-to-discrete assembly is inferred from the scalar wave example.

contents.name: Leapfrog from Centered Differences
contents.support: The algorithm records the integer electric states and half-integer magnetic states, with the two explicit updates justified by the exact matrix system. The source's scalar centered stencil is not used as a proof premise.

contents.name: Stability of the Leapfrog Method
contents.support: The theorem proves its strict finite-matrix norm threshold using a modified energy and singular modes. The source's one-dimensional Fourier threshold is treated as context and is not substituted for the matrix proof.

contents.name: Wave Equation in Higher Dimensions
contents.reason: The higher-dimensional continuous wave equation and its fundamental solution are outside this abstract finite-matrix pair and supply no premise for the stated energy identity.

contents.name: Leapfrog Method in Higher Dimensions
contents.reason: Grid-dependent multidimensional Fourier symbols and spatial CFL constants are not claimed; this pair uses the operator norm of arbitrary finite compatible matrices.

contents.name: Energy identity for symmetric first-order systems
contents.support: The matrix theorem supplies a complete finite-dimensional energy balance by differentiating its stated quadratic form and cancelling the two coupling terms. The source's PDE boundary-flux assumptions are not imported.

contents.name: Maxwell's Equations on a staggered grid
contents.support: The source relates the Yee update to staggered electric and magnetic time levels. This item states only the finite algebraic procedure and does not assert a mesh realization.

contents.name: Problem Set 5.3
contents.reason: The exercises are prompts rather than additional established results needed by this page; every claim used here is stated and proved in the authored carriers.

sources.title: J. Zank, Topics in Finite Elements, Part I: Wave Equation, University of Vienna lecture notes
sources.locator: Chapter 2, §2.3, Leapfrog Method; Definition 2.9, Lemma 2.10, Remark 2.11, Theorems 2.12 and 2.14, PDF pp. 13–17. Read the full discrete-energy definition, CFL positivity argument, energy-conservation proof, and stability statement with its finite-element hypotheses.

contents.name: Definition 2.9: discrete energy of the leapfrog method
contents.support: The matrix theorem defines and proves its own modified energy, including the mixed half-step term. Zank's finite-element energy has different state spaces and is not copied as the matrix formula.

contents.name: Lemma 2.10: CFL condition makes the finite-element leapfrog energy nonnegative
contents.support: The strict positive-energy argument is developed for the finite matrix system using Cauchy–Schwarz and the induced matrix norm. Zank's mesh inverse inequality and shape-regularity hypotheses are not needed or claimed.

contents.name: Remark 2.11: weaker finite-element CFL condition
contents.reason: This weaker condition depends on the finite-element inverse inequality and its mesh constants, none of which belongs to the abstract matrix statement or its proof.

contents.name: Theorem 2.12: energy conservation of the leapfrog method
contents.support: The theorem proves exact conservation of the modified finite-matrix energy by expanding the staggered update, with all matrix identities written out locally.

contents.name: Remark 2.13: energy conservation under the weaker CFL condition
contents.reason: The remark depends on the separate finite-element inverse-inequality condition and does not strengthen or qualify the finite-matrix threshold proved here.

contents.name: Theorem 2.14: stability of the finite-element leapfrog method
contents.reason: Its conclusion is an H1 and L2 bound for a mesh-discretized wave equation with regularity and CFL hypotheses; this pair proves no continuum or mesh error estimate.
